analysis.title: South Korea Technology: Semiconductors - Memory: TrendForce memory expert session reaffirming strong 2027 DRAM/HBM outlook
key_insights: GS hosted a TrendForce memory expert webinar on October 27, 2026 covering the DRAM and HBM markets. GS reiterates Buy on Samsung Electronics (common and preference) and SK Hynix.

TrendForce expects DRAM supply to stay tight throughout 2027. Robust server demand and limited supply additions should support further ASP increases over the next several quarters despite weaker consumer demand. TrendForce expects DRAM pricing to keep rising until 1H28.

TrendForce said long-term agreement (LTA) coverage of up to 60-70% could lead to more moderate price increases in 2027. Incremental demand beyond committed volumes could still be negotiated at higher prices.

TrendForce expects blended HBM ASP to rise 122% yoy to US$3.7/Gb in 2027, driving HBM industry revenue growth of more than 230% yoy to exceed $200bn. GS says this is consistent with its own estimate of 100-160% yoy HBM ASP growth for the major suppliers next year.

TrendForce sees wide HBM4 price variance by supplier and customer in 2027: the high end could exceed US$5/Gb and the low end is closer to US$3/Gb. It believes 8-hi HBM4 could command a 5-10% per-bit premium over 12-hi because of higher base-die cost per memory unit. HBM4E pricing next year could be materially higher than HBM4.

TrendForce sees meaningful DRAM capacity additions as unlikely before 2028 despite aggressive capex plans, because of cleanroom constraints and long equipment lead times. Each Korean supplier could add 80-100K WPM in 2027, but Samsung's incremental capacity is expected to go largely to HBM. Conventional DRAM bit growth therefore depends mainly on technology migration.
TrendForce said equipment availability may begin improving from 2H27, letting new fabs contribute more supply from 2028. Suppliers could still control expansion plans based on the demand outlook.

TrendForce said Google is becoming a more important driver of HBM demand. A rising TPU mix should support HBM3E bit demand next year, so HBM demand broadens across generations rather than concentrating on HBM4/4E. Because of its price premium, HBM4 is expected to make up close to 60% of HBM industry revenue in 2027.

TrendForce sees limited medium-term competitive risk from Chinese HBM suppliers, citing a considerable gap in technology and yield versus the leading suppliers. It expects Chinese suppliers to hold less than 2% of the HBM market in 2027, with JHICC focused on HBM2E and CXMT targeting HBM3/3E.

market_movers.rationale: GS reiterates Buy on Samsung Electronics, with a 12m EV/EBITDA-based SOTP target price of W500,000 for the common share and W380,000 for the preference share. Samsung is on the Conviction List (CL). Samsung's incremental 2027 capacity is expected to go largely to HBM.

GS reiterates Buy on SK Hynix, with a 12m target price of W3,500,000 based on a 9.0X target P/E on 2026E/27E average earnings. TrendForce's outlook for DRAM and HBM pricing through 2027 supports the call.

sector_views.rationale: Tight DRAM supply, rising DRAM and HBM ASPs through 2027, and limited capacity additions before 2028 support memory suppliers. GS keeps Buy ratings on Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix.

risk_factors: Samsung: major deterioration in memory supply/demand, sharp contraction in smartphone margins, and mobile OLED market share loss.

SK Hynix: major deterioration in memory supply/demand and delay in technology migration, weaker smartphone/PC/server demand hurting conventional memory, Samsung's HBM progress taking share, and lower AI-related capex reducing HBM demand.
TrendForce noted suppliers could control capacity expansion plans based on the demand outlook.
Consumer demand is weaker, which TrendForce expects server demand to offset.
geopolitical: The report discusses Chinese HBM suppliers (JHICC and CXMT) as a medium-term competitive risk. TrendForce sees that risk as limited.
